case: Criminal investigation into alleged violations of the restrictions on party finances ('Silvergate'), 2012
type: criminal investigation (Michal as suspect); terminated before any charge
description: On 22 May 2012 the State Prosecutor's Office opened criminal proceedings under the Penal Code provision on violating restrictions on a political party's economic activities or assets, to check Silver Meikar's claim that the Reform Party had accepted money of unknown origin registered as members' donations, at the suggestion of Michal, then secretary general (see polemics). In the summer of 2012 the prosecutor declared Michal, then Minister of Justice, and Reform member Kalev Lillo suspects; according to The Baltic Times the suspicion concerned violating rules on a party's economic activities or property and, on conviction, would have carried a financial penalty. Reform members Kalle Palling and Priit Kallakas were also suspects, and two people were suspected under bribery provisions (The Baltic Course). Michal denied the allegations throughout.
outcome: In October 2012 the State Prosecutor's Office closed the case without charges: the evidence was enough to create a suspicion but not to compile a convincing charge. Leading State Prosecutor Heili Sepp said every act came down to 'word against word' and that the 2–4 years between the events and the first testimony made the witnesses' allegations impossible to verify.
court: State Prosecutor's Office (Riigiprokuratuur), pre-trial investigation; no court proceedings
presumption_note: Michal was a suspect in a pre-trial investigation that was closed without charges; he denied the allegations and was never charged or tried. He is presumed innocent.
key_facts: Proceedings opened 22 May 2012 under the Penal Code provision on party finances
Michal and Kalev Lillo declared suspects in summer 2012
Case closed without charges in October 2012 for insufficient evidence
